To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the solubility and stability of amorphous dispersions of acetaminophens and naproxen can be predicted with the PC-SAFT and Flory-Huggin models, and that the stability of amorphorous solid dispersions of acetamiphen can be predicted with both models, but the stability of amporphorous solid dispersions containing naproxen can only be predicted with PC-SAFT.
the solubility and stability of amorphous acetaminophen in the excipients PVP K25 (K25) and polyvinylpyrrolidonco-co-vinylacetate (PVPVA) was predicted by PC-SAFT, FH, and an empirical model.
the solubility models PC-SAFT and Flory-Huggin (FH) are able to predict the long-term physical stabilities of amorphous acetaminophen- and naproxen-PVP and PVPVA ASD formulations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the physical stability of ASDs and the impact of RH on API solubility.
the long-term physical stabilization of ASDs.
the development of a modeling approach that can be used for the prediction of the physical stability of ASDs at different RH conditions and temperatures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PC-SAFT is superior to FH for modeling the solubility and stability of ASD.
FH and PC-SAFT are both suitable for the calculation of the API solubilities in PVP K30 and PVPVA 64.
PC-SAFT is able to predict the physical stability of PVP-ASD formulations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

PC-SAFT is able to describe the solubility and the physical stability of ASDs in the investigated polymers at humid conditions, which is a promising approach to predict the physical stability of other ASD formulations.
PC-SAFT is a suitable approach to model the API solubilities in the polymers and the glass transition temperature of dry ASD.
PC-SAFT can be used as a reliable model to predict the long-term physical and chemical stability of ASD.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the solubility models can predict the long-term stability of ASDs, but only if the solubility is calculated at temperatures that are higher than room temperature.
the solubility models FH and PC-SAFT can be used to predict the long-term physical behavior of ASD formulations at room temperature and at humid conditions.
the long-term stability of ASD formulations cannot be reliably predicted with PC-SAFT and that FH is not applicable to PVP K25 at all.
